title: Standardized patient: sudden weakness
intro: A simulation: an overhead page, "Code stroke, Clinical Skills Room 1." Mrs. Eleanor Hayes, 76, and her husband. The clock on the wall is running.

steps.say: Mrs. Hayes sits in a wheelchair, her left arm limp in her lap, the left side of her mouth drooping. Her husband stands behind her, still holding her handbag.

options.text: Introduce yourself, then ask straight away: "When was she last completely normal?"
options.reply: "Quarter past ten. We were doing the crossword," says Mr. Hayes. The clock reads 11:00.

options.text: Start a full past medical history, from childhood.
options.reply: Minutes go by. The coordinator makes a note.

options.text: Examine her first, without introducing yourself.
options.reply: Mr. Hayes watches, confused about who you are.

choice.lesson: In a suspected stroke, the time last known well comes first: it decides the treatment

history.patient: Mrs. Eleanor Hayes, 76, with her husband
history.opening: Mr. Hayes: "She just dropped her teacup, and her face went funny."

items.ask: Exactly when was she last known to be well?
items.answer: "At 10:15 we were doing the crossword. At 10:30 she dropped the cup."
"Her face dropped on the left, and her left arm just fell."

items.ask: Does she have diabetes? Has she eaten?
Does she take a blood thinner?
items.answer: "No. Just aspirin, and a blood pressure pill."

items.ask: Any recent surgery, bleeding or head injury?
How was she day to day before this?
items.answer: "Completely independent. She drives, gardens and beats me at chess."
"The nurse said her pulse was irregular last month. They were going to do a heart tracing."

maneuvers.name: Vital signs
maneuvers.finding: BP 176/94, HR 92 and irregularly irregular, SpO₂ 97%, temperature normal.

maneuvers.name: Ask her to smile and raise her eyebrows
maneuvers.finding: The lower left face droops; her forehead wrinkles normally on both sides.

maneuvers.name: Arm drift
maneuvers.finding: Her left arm drifts down and hits the bed within ten seconds.

maneuvers.name: Speech
maneuvers.finding: Slightly slurred, but the words are right and she understands everything.

maneuvers.name: Visual fields
maneuvers.finding: She misses your fingers on her left side, in both eyes.

maneuvers.name: Touch both hands at once
maneuvers.finding: She feels only the right: left-sided extinction. She doesn't seem aware of her weakness.

maneuvers.name: Gaze
maneuvers.finding: Her eyes rest looking to the right.

steps.question: sp_weak_localize_01
steps.lead: The stroke fellow arrives. "Where is it?"

choice.prompt: As she's wheeled out to the CT scanner, Mr. Hayes grabs your sleeve. "Is she going to be all right?"

options.text: "It looks like a stroke, and she's getting here fast, which is the best thing that could have happened. The stroke team will talk with you as soon as the scan is done. Come with me: I'll show you where to wait."
options.reply: He nods, and follows you, still holding her handbag.
He believes you. You can't know that.
He sits down alone in the empty room.

choice.lesson: Be honest, give the family something true to hold on to, and don't leave them alone

feedback: "Fast and methodical. You'd have got her to the scanner well inside the target time."
"Good. The time last known well first, then glucose, then the scan."
"Review the code-stroke steps. Time is brain."
